subject.title: Windows: multiple gateway-down failure modes (kill-and-rebind restart loop, config-edit no-relaunch, browser launch crash, blocking pricing fetches)

question: Should this broad Windows gateway-down report remain the canonical umbrella while maintainers split the proven subissues into scoped fixes, or should one narrower existing Windows restart issue become canonical for the lifecycle portion?
rationale: Source inspection proves some failures but not all eight, and choosing the canonical split affects product behavior for gateway ensure/start semantics, Windows supervisor expectations, and pricing defaults.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split fixes
options.body: Keep this issue open as the P0 umbrella, require live Windows proof for lifecycle/browser claims, and create or route scoped repair work for each proven subissue.

options.title: Promote a narrower lifecycle canonical
options.body: Use an existing Windows restart issue as the canonical owner for start/restart behavior and keep this issue only for the remaining config, pricing, and browser failures.

options.title: Pause pending live repro
options.body: Do no implementation work until a maintainer or trusted tester reproduces the Windows Scheduled Task and Edge crash paths on current main.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split fixes
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the P0 umbrella, require live Windows proof for lifecycle/browser claims, and create or route scoped repair work for each proven subissue.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-main history signal across gateway lifecycle, stale-process cleanup, pricing, and respawn code.
